annotation.authors_or_issuer: China (submission to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.summary_en: China's April 2018 working paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts sets out its preliminary position on lethal autonomous weapons systems: a narrow definition of LAWS by five characteristics, clarification of human-machine interaction, caution against indiscriminate use, IHL applicability, and avoiding prejudgments that impede AI development.
annotation.title_clean: CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.7 – Position Paper on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (China)
annotation.title_en: CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.7 – Position Paper on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (China)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts, Geneva
key_provisions_or_claims: LAWS should be understood as fully autonomous lethal systems with five characteristics: lethality, autonomy, non-terminability, indiscriminate effect, evolution
Supports agreeing a definition starting from technical characteristics
Concepts such as meaningful human control need further clarification
LAWS are subject to IHL but distinction, proportionality and accountability are doubtful
Calls for precaution and avoiding indiscriminate use against civilians, without prejudging outcomes that impede AI development
